# dsh-superagent
English | 简体中文

> **Unofficial fork — not a DeepSeek product.** This repository is an independent fork of
> deepseek

-ai/dsh-superagent-prototype, maintained by
> samanhappy. Neither DeepSeek nor the DeepSeek Harness

team maintains, endorses or supports this fork.
> The upstream code is MIT-licensed, © 2026 DeepSeek

Harness Team; the changes and additions in this fork are
> © 2026 samanhappy, under the same licenc

the changes and additions in this fork are
> © 2026 samanhappy, under the same licence. See NOTICE.
> **The upstream caveat still applies.** The prototype describes itself as a "research prototype for

reference only,
> not an official DeepSeek product", written largely by coding agents, and not prod

uction-ready software. This fork
> does not turn it into a hardened service; it is a step toward run

ning it every day in one team, with the
> limitations that come with that.
dsh-superagent is a proactive coding agent for the repositories a team watches, packaged as a bundle
for DeepSeek Harness. It listens to GitHub and, optionally, GitLab, Feishu, PingCode, WeCom and WeC
hat. When someone allowed asks the agent for work, it opens a work item, works on it in its own agen
t session and directory, and answers in the original conversation, for example with a pull request.
A web panel shows what needs a person.
It is also a way of working with an agent: **take as little human attention as possible, and give as
much value as possible.** An agent that can act for a whole team can also waste a whole team's atte
ntion, so it acts only when asked or when a rule the team wrote allows it, and speaks only when some
one must act or can use a result. docs/000-philosophy.md explains the principle and what it asks of
or can use a result. docs/000-philosophy.md explains the principle and what it asks of the operator.
## Screenshots
The management panel on a fresh install, before any credential is configured: the deployment checks
that gate taking work, the six Sources, and where each Source is set up.
## What this fork is for
The upstream project is a reference implementation: one GitHub repository, one optional Feishu sourc
e, and code meant to be read and adapted. This fork keeps that design and takes it toward a state wh
ere a team can install it as a normal DeepSeek Harness plugin, leave it running, and point it at the
channels the team already uses.
Concretely, on top of upstream:
- **Install once and get every Source.** Each Source is a separate plugin row in cordis.patch.yml wi
th its own `*-watch` entry in `package.json`, so a single `dsh plugin add "link:$PWD"` installs the
whole bundle. Profiles can drop a Source by disabling its row; a Source that is installed but unconf

igured stays paused and reports why.
- **More Sources than upstream.** GitLab (through `glab`: insta
nce host, projects, polling, observe switches for issues, merge requests and comments); PingCode (th
rough the local PingCode skill and its user token: projects resolved by ID, identifier or name, repl
ies as work-item comments); WeCom (an intelligent robot over one long connection per bot: reconnect
with backoff, markdown replies, conversation-window context, and a clear error when another client t
akes the bot over); WeChat (via iLink, through a QR-code login in the panel, long polling for direct
messages, replies in the same conversation). GitLab, PingCode and WeCom ship a Skill for workers; a

ll four come with panel settings, setup verification, documentation and tests.
- **Day-two operation
, not just a demo.** Setup re-checks each configured Source (repository and push access, GitLab role
and credentials per project, PingCode token and projects, WeCom credentials, WeChat token) and a fa
iling Source disables only itself; Sources report health and back off instead of hammering; saving a
card restarts the service when it must; the panel is bilingual (English/Chinese) and documents ever

y configuration field in place.
- **A regression net while the core changes.** About 1,300 tests acr
oss 65 files, plus documentation tests that keep the module table, the test table and every local li
nk honest, run in CI on every push and pull request.
## Compatibility risk
This fork tracks a public research prototype, so treat compatibility as a moving target rather than
tracks a public research prototype, so treat compatibility as a moving target rather than a promise:
- **Upstream may keep changing.** If `deepseek-ai/dsh-superagent-prototype` keeps evolving, its next
commits touch the same files this fork extends — `cordis.patch.yml`, the preset rows, the prompt se
ctions, the panel, `package.json` exports, `docs/`, `tests/`. Rebasing onto those changes will confl

ict, and conflicts in prompt or preset code can change agent behaviour quietly.
- **DeepSeek Harness
is alpha and pinned.** Peer dependencies require `^0.2.1-alpha.2` and the dev dependencies are pinn
ed to it. The published bundle is also smoke-tested against the `0.2.2-rc.1` desktop app (install, b
oot and panel render); treat every further DSH release as unverified until it is tested. New DSH rel
eases may change the services these Sources call and the bundle patch format; porting those changes

is manual work here, and this fork will lag upstream until it is done.
- **A hard fork drifts both w
ays.** Upstream bug fixes and security fixes do not arrive automatically, and improvements made here
(the four added Sources in particular) are unlikely to be upstreamed by the upstream team. There is

no guarantee that the two stay compatible.
- **No wire-level compatibility promise.** Source config
uration and the state database belong to this fork; the database schema moves with the code, and a s
tate directory migrated by a newer version cannot be opened by an older one. Back up `stateDir` befo
re upgrading, as docs/006-deployment.md says.
The practical stance: keep additions additive, rebase onto upstream regularly, treat each DSH upgrad
e as a migration with a backup, and read the upstream changes before merging. If you need long-term
stability more than new Sources, pin a commit of either repository and test before moving.
## Security
Do not open a public issue for a vulnerability. SECURITY.md explains how to report one privately and
what this software assumes about the machine it runs on.
